primarySchoolChemistrySources.title: Synthesis of aspirin on a microscale
primarySchoolChemistrySources.usedFacts: School16–18 synthesis from salicylic acid and ethanoic anhydride with phosphoric acid;70–80°C bath15min, microscale reagents, crystallisation and ethanol/water recrystallisation; fume cupboard and splash goggles.
primarySchoolChemistrySources.authorAdaptations: Measured delivery-mass record, controlled cooling before supervised water quench, explicit partitioned mass ledger, drying criterion and own-sample downstream tests are author design additions requiring independent review.

primarySchoolChemistrySources.title: Analysis of aspirin tablets on a microscale
primarySchoolChemistrySources.usedFacts: Free salicylic acid gives Fe(III) colour; compare with known standards and relate salicylic acid mass to weighed sample mass.1:1 ethanol/water solvent,0.1mol/L iron(III) nitrate and salicylic stock/working dilution are documented.
primarySchoolChemistrySources.authorAdaptations: Original synthesis powder replaces tablets; volumetric equal-ASA reference matrix, volumetric aliquots, timed readings, bracketing, spike and validity conditions are explicit unapproved author adaptations.

primarySchoolChemistrySources.title: The melting point of aspirin
primarySchoolChemistrySources.usedFacts: Compare dry crude/purified aspirin melting intervals; narrow versus depressed/broadened melting supports a limited purity assessment. Pure aspirin reference138–140°C is in the accompanying student sheet.
primarySchoolChemistrySources.authorAdaptations: Electric apparatus, presealed tubes, slow approach and simultaneous pure/mixed reference observations; interpretation remains bounded, not a purity certificate.

primarySchoolChemistrySources.title: The preparation of aspirin
primarySchoolChemistrySources.usedFacts: Unreacted salicylic acid and hydrolysis products can contaminate aspirin. Wet isolated solid can strongly inflate apparent mass; drying and mass-based interpretation matter.
primarySchoolChemistrySources.authorAdaptations: No claim that colour or melting alone detects all water, acid or by-products.
